sentence: Make this description shorter by omitting the relative word: The flat that we viewed yesterday has a balcony.
setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves the meaning in standard written English.
taskText: Make this description shorter by omitting the relative word: The flat that we viewed yesterday has a balcony.
text: Choose the sentence that preserves the meaning in standard written English. Make this description shorter by omitting the relative word: The flat that we viewed yesterday has a balcony.
options: The flat we viewing yesterday has a balcony.
The flat we viewed it yesterday has a balcony.
The flat we viewed yesterday has a balcony.
The flat was viewed yesterday has a balcony.
answer: The flat we viewed yesterday has a balcony.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3161:Omitting an object relative pronoun
explanation: That is the object of viewed, so it can be omitted while we remains the subject.

rationales.The flat we viewed yesterday has a balco: That is the object of viewed, so it can be omitted while we remains the subject.
rationales.The flat we viewing yesterday has a balc: Viewing needs an auxiliary after we; simply omitting that leaves the finite verb viewed unchanged.
rationales.The flat we viewed it yesterday has a ba: The flat is already the understood object of viewed; adding it repeats that object.
rationales.The flat was viewed yesterday has a balc: Replacing the relative with was viewed leaves two finite predicates without a link and loses the subject we.

sentence: Describe the volunteers who organized the food collection.
setupText: Choose the grammatically correct sentence in standard written English.
taskText: Describe the volunteers who organized the food collection.
text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence in standard written English. Describe the volunteers who organized the food collection.
options: The volunteers they organized the collection thanked the donors.
The volunteers organized the collection thanked the donors.
The volunteers who organized the collection thanked the donors.
The volunteers who they organized the collection thanked the donors.
answer: The volunteers who organized the collection thanked the donors.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3162:Keeping a subject relative pronoun
explanation: Who is the subject of organized and links that action to volunteers; thanked is the main verb.

rationales.The volunteers they organized the collec: They does not connect the description to volunteers and leaves two clauses without a suitable link.
rationales.The volunteers organized the collection: The subject relative who cannot simply be omitted before organized in this sentence.
rationales.The volunteers who organized the collect: Who is the subject of organized and links that action to volunteers; thanked is the main verb.
rationales.The volunteers who they organized the co: Who already supplies the subject of organized, so they repeats it.

sentence: I interviewed a candidate. The candidate had managed a busy restaurant.
setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves both facts.
taskText: I interviewed a candidate. The candidate had managed a busy restaurant.
text: Choose the sentence that preserves both facts. I interviewed a candidate. The candidate had managed a busy restaurant.
options: The candidate who interviewed me had managed a busy restaurant.
The candidate I interviewed had managed a busy restaurant.
I had managed the restaurant where the candidate interviewed me.
The candidate I interviewed wanted to manage a busy restaurant.
answer: The candidate I interviewed had managed a busy restaurant.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3163:Combining facts with an object relative
explanation: I interviewed identifies the candidate as the interviewee; had managed preserves the earlier experience.

rationales.The candidate who interviewed me had man: This reverses the interview roles: the candidate becomes the interviewer.
rationales.The candidate I interviewed had managed: I interviewed identifies the candidate as the interviewee; had managed preserves the earlier experience.
rationales.I had managed the restaurant where the c: This makes the speaker the restaurant manager and changes the interview location and roles.
rationales.The candidate I interviewed wanted to ma: Wanting to manage a restaurant does not preserve the candidate's actual earlier experience.

sentence: The tenant has asked the landlord for help. The tenant's kitchen ceiling leaks.
setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves both facts.
taskText: The tenant has asked the landlord for help. The tenant's kitchen ceiling leaks.
text: Choose the sentence that preserves both facts. The tenant has asked the landlord for help. The tenant's kitchen ceiling leaks.
options: The tenant whose ceiling was repaired has asked for help.
The tenant whose kitchen ceiling leaks has asked for help.
The landlord whose kitchen ceiling leaks has asked for help.
The tenant whose kitchen ceiling leaks has offered to help.
answer: The tenant whose kitchen ceiling leaks has asked for help.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3164:Combining ownership with a main action
explanation: Whose links the kitchen ceiling to the tenant, and has asked preserves the tenant's request.

rationales.The tenant whose ceiling was repaired ha: Was repaired replaces the current leak with a completed repair.
rationales.The landlord whose kitchen ceiling leaks: This transfers both the leaking kitchen and the request to the landlord.
rationales.The tenant whose kitchen ceiling leaks h: Offering help changes the tenant from someone requesting help to someone providing it.
Whose links the kitchen ceiling to the tenant, and has asked preserves the tenant's request.

sentence: We first met on a particular day. I will never forget that day.
setupText: Choose the sentence that describes the day of the meeting, not a day someone remembered or chose.
taskText: We first met on a particular day. I will never forget that day.
text: Choose the sentence that describes the day of the meeting, not a day someone remembered or chose. We first met on a particular day. I will never forget that day.
options: I'll never forget the day that we chose for our first meeting.
I'll never forget the day that you remembered.
I'll never forget the day before we first met.
I'll never forget the day when we first met.
answer: I'll never forget the day when we first met.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3165:Time relative versus object description of a day
explanation: When connects the day to the time of the first meeting.

rationales.I'll never forget the day when we first: When connects the day to the time of the first meeting.
rationales.I'll never forget the day that we chose: Choosing a meeting day is not the same event as actually meeting on that day.
rationales.I'll never forget the day that you remem: This identifies the day through your memory, without saying it was when we first met.
rationales.I'll never forget the day before we firs: Before places the remembered day earlier than the meeting, changing the relationship.

sentence: Describe a restaurant by saying that we had lunch there.
setupText: Choose the grammatically correct sentence in standard written English.
taskText: Describe a restaurant by saying that we had lunch there.
text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence in standard written English. Describe a restaurant by saying that we had lunch there.
options: The restaurant where we had lunch overlooks the river.
The restaurant where we had lunch there overlooks the river.
The restaurant which we had lunch overlooks the river.
The restaurant whose we had lunch overlooks the river.
answer: The restaurant where we had lunch overlooks the river.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3166:Place relative without redundant there
explanation: Where replaces in that restaurant and needs no extra there.

rationales.The restaurant where we had lunch there: Where already expresses the location of lunch, so there repeats that location.
rationales.The restaurant which we had lunch overlo: We had lunch in a restaurant; which alone does not supply the necessary location relationship.
rationales.The restaurant where we had lunch overlo: Where replaces in that restaurant and needs no extra there.
rationales.The restaurant whose we had lunch overlo: Whose introduces a possessed noun, not the location of we had lunch.

sentence: The outdoor class was cancelled because the instructor was ill.
setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves the reason for cancelling.
taskText: The outdoor class was cancelled because the instructor was ill.
text: Choose the sentence that preserves the reason for cancelling. The outdoor class was cancelled because the instructor was ill.
options: The instructor who cancelled the class became ill afterward.
The class that made the instructor ill was cancelled.
The instructor whose class was cancelled felt better.
The reason why the class was cancelled was the instructor's illness.
answer: The reason why the class was cancelled was the instructor's illness.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3167:Recasting a cause with the reason why
explanation: The reason why names the action being explained, and illness supplies its cause.

rationales.The instructor who cancelled the class b: This changes the order and does not preserve illness as the cause of cancellation.
rationales.The reason why the class was cancelled w: The reason why names the action being explained, and illness supplies its cause.
rationales.The class that made the instructor ill w: This makes the class the cause of the illness, reversing the original causal relationship.
rationales.The instructor whose class was cancelled: Feeling better is new information and does not state why the cancellation happened.

sentence: The manager thanked the staff who had stayed late. Which group does the relative clause identify?
setupText: Choose the option that preserves the intended group.
taskText: The manager thanked the staff who had stayed late. Which group does the relative clause identify?
text: Choose the option that preserves the intended group. The manager thanked the staff who had stayed late. Which group does the relative clause identify?
options: Staff who remained after their usual hours
Staff whose manager stayed late
Staff whom the manager asked to stay late
Staff who thanked the manager afterward
answer: Staff who remained after their usual hours
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3168:A relative clause restricts a group by a completed action
explanation: Who had stayed late restricts staff to those who remained beyond their usual working time.

rationales.Staff whose manager stayed late: Who had stayed late describes the staff's action, not the manager's.
rationales.Staff whom the manager asked to stay lat: The sentence says they stayed; it does not say the manager asked them to.
rationales.Staff who thanked the manager afterward: The manager thanked the staff, so this reverses the direction of thanks.
rationales.Staff who remained after their usual hou: Who had stayed late restricts staff to those who remained beyond their usual working time.

sentence: Preserve the direction of the loan in a relative-clause description.
setupText: Choose the sentence that says the speaker lent the book to Rosa.
taskText: Preserve the direction of the loan in a relative-clause description.
text: Choose the sentence that says the speaker lent the book to Rosa. Preserve the direction of the loan in a relative-clause description.
options: The book Rosa lent me is about urban gardens.
The book Rosa borrowed from the library is about urban gardens.
The book I lent Rosa is about urban gardens.
The book I borrowed from Rosa is about urban gardens.
answer: The book I lent Rosa is about urban gardens.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3169:Interpreting two objects in a contact relative
explanation: I is the lender and Rosa the recipient inside the relative clause I lent Rosa.

rationales.The book I lent Rosa is about urban gard: I is the lender and Rosa the recipient inside the relative clause I lent Rosa.
rationales.The book Rosa lent me is about urban gar: Rosa becomes the lender here, reversing the intended loan.
rationales.The book Rosa borrowed from the library: This makes the library the source of Rosa's book instead of the speaker.
rationales.The book I borrowed from Rosa is about u: Borrowed from Rosa makes the speaker the recipient rather than the lender.

sentence: I use a small knife to open parcels. That knife is missing.
setupText: Choose the description that preserves the missing tool's use.
taskText: I use a small knife to open parcels. That knife is missing.
text: Choose the description that preserves the missing tool's use. I use a small knife to open parcels. That knife is missing.
options: The knife that arrived in the parcel is missing.
The knife I open parcels with is missing.
The knife that I use to cut bread is missing.
The parcel I keep the knife in is missing.
answer: The knife I open parcels with is missing.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3170:Describing an instrument with a final preposition
explanation: With links the knife to opening parcels; the object relative pronoun can be omitted before I.

rationales.The knife that arrived in the parcel is: The original identifies the knife by its use, not by how it arrived.
rationales.The knife that I use to cut bread is mis: Cutting bread changes the stated purpose of the knife.
rationales.The knife I open parcels with is missing: With links the knife to opening parcels; the object relative pronoun can be omitted before I.
rationales.The parcel I keep the knife in is missin: This says the parcel is missing and describes storage, changing both the missing object and the relationship.

sentence: The station is beside the stadium. It has two entrances.
setupText: Choose the sentence that describes a station's location, not a visit to it.
taskText: The station is beside the stadium. It has two entrances.
text: Choose the sentence that describes a station's location, not a visit to it. The station is beside the stadium. It has two entrances.
options: The station that we visited has two entrances.
The stadium beside the station has two entrances.
The station that has two entrances is beside the theatre.
The station that stands beside the stadium has two entrances.
answer: The station that stands beside the stadium has two entrances.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3171:A place noun as subject of a relative clause
explanation: That stands beside the stadium describes the station's location; the main clause preserves its two entrances.

rationales.The station that we visited has two entr: This identifies the station through a visit and omits its location beside the stadium.
rationales.The station that stands beside the stadi: That stands beside the stadium describes the station's location; the main clause preserves its two entrances.
rationales.The stadium beside the station has two e: This gives the stadium two entrances instead of the station.
rationales.The station that has two entrances is be: The theatre replaces the stadium and changes the stated location.

sentence: Maya left the course. Nobody knows why.
setupText: Choose the sentence that keeps the reason unknown and the departure certain.
taskText: Maya left the course. Nobody knows why.
text: Choose the sentence that keeps the reason unknown and the departure certain. Maya left the course. Nobody knows why.
options: Nobody knows the course that Maya left.
Nobody knows the reason why Maya left the course.
Maya knows the reason why nobody left the course.
Nobody knows whether Maya left the course.
answer: Nobody knows the reason why Maya left the course.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3172:Unknown reason versus uncertain event
explanation: The reason why identifies the missing explanation while preserving the fact that Maya left.

This makes the identity of the course unknown, not the reason for leaving.
rationales.Maya knows the reason why nobody left th: This changes both who knows and who left; the original says Maya left.
rationales.Nobody knows whether Maya left the cours: Whether makes the departure itself uncertain, although the original reports it as a fact.
rationales.Nobody knows the reason why Maya left th: The reason why identifies the missing explanation while preserving the fact that Maya left.

sentence: Add the information that Carlos speaks Arabic to the statement that he will meet the guests.
setupText: Choose the grammatically correct sentence in standard written English.
taskText: Add the information that Carlos speaks Arabic to the statement that he will meet the guests.
text: Choose the grammatically correct sentence in standard written English. Add the information that Carlos speaks Arabic to the statement that he will meet the guests.
options: Carlos, who speaks Arabic, will meet the guests.
Carlos, that speaks Arabic, will meet the guests.
Carlos, speaks Arabic, will meet the guests.
Carlos, who he speaks Arabic, will meet the guests.
answer: Carlos, who speaks Arabic, will meet the guests.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3173:A basic non-defining person relative
explanation: Who introduces extra information about the named person between commas.

rationales.Carlos, who speaks Arabic, will meet the: Who introduces extra information about the named person between commas.
rationales.Carlos, that speaks Arabic, will meet th: That is not used for this comma-separated supplementary relative in standard written English.
rationales.Carlos, speaks Arabic, will meet the gue: A finite supplementary relative needs its subject who; the commas do not supply it.
rationales.Carlos, who he speaks Arabic, will meet: Who already serves as the subject of speaks, making he redundant.

sentence: A company uses a green logo. That company repairs household appliances.
setupText: Choose the sentence that preserves the relationship between the company and its logo.
taskText: A company uses a green logo. That company repairs household appliances.
text: Choose the sentence that preserves the relationship between the company and its logo. A company uses a green logo. That company repairs household appliances.
options: The company whose logo is green makes household appliances.
The company whose appliances are green repairs household goods.
The company whose logo is green repairs household appliances.
The company whose logo was redesigned sells household appliances.
answer: The company whose logo is green repairs household appliances.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3174:Whose with an organization
explanation: Whose links the logo to the company; organizations, as well as people, can have whose descriptions.

rationales.The company whose logo is green makes ho: Makes changes the company's work from repairing appliances to manufacturing them.
rationales.The company whose appliances are green r: This attaches the colour to the appliances, not to the logo.
rationales.The company whose logo is green repairs: Whose links the logo to the company; organizations, as well as people, can have whose descriptions.
rationales.The company whose logo was redesigned se: This substitutes redesign for the stated colour and selling for repairing.

sentence: Everything ___ was left in the locker has been collected.
setupText: Choose the word that completes the sentence grammatically in standard written English.
taskText: Everything ___ was left in the locker has been collected.
text: Choose the word that completes the sentence grammatically in standard written English. Everything ___ was left in the locker has been collected.
options: what
that
who
whose
answer: that
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3175:That after everything versus fused what
explanation: That links the remaining possessions to was left; it is the subject of the relative clause.

rationales.what: Everything already supplies the antecedent; what cannot follow it as the relative pronoun here.
rationales.that: That links the remaining possessions to was left; it is the subject of the relative clause.
rationales.who: Who refers to people, not the possessions represented by everything.
rationales.whose: Whose requires a following possessed noun and cannot act alone as this subject.

sentence: We stayed in a village. A ferry leaves from that village every morning.
setupText: Choose the description that preserves both facts.
taskText: We stayed in a village. A ferry leaves from that village every morning.
text: Choose the description that preserves both facts. We stayed in a village. A ferry leaves from that village every morning.
options: The village where we stayed receives a ferry every evening.
We stayed on the ferry that serves the village each morning.
A ferry leaves every morning from the village where we stayed.
The village that we left receives a ferry every morning.
answer: A ferry leaves every morning from the village where we stayed.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3176:A place relative inside a prepositional phrase
explanation: Where we stayed identifies the village, and from makes that village the ferry's departure point.

rationales.The village where we stayed receives a f: This changes a morning departure into an evening arrival.
rationales.We stayed on the ferry that serves the v: This puts our accommodation on the ferry, not in the village.
rationales.The village that we left receives a ferr: This substitutes our departure for our stay and a ferry arrival for its departure.
rationales.A ferry leaves every morning from the vi: Where we stayed identifies the village, and from makes that village the ferry's departure point.

sentence: The colleague to whom I sent the timetable has replied.
setupText: Choose the version that preserves the meaning in ordinary English.
taskText: The colleague to whom I sent the timetable has replied.
text: Choose the version that preserves the meaning in ordinary English. The colleague to whom I sent the timetable has replied.
options: The colleague I sent the timetable to has replied.
The colleague who sent me the timetable has replied.
The colleague whose timetable I replied to has sent it.
The timetable that my colleague sent has been replied to.
answer: The colleague I sent the timetable to has replied.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3177:Fronted preposition to ordinary final-preposition relative
explanation: The preposition moves to the end, and the object relative can be omitted: I sent the timetable to that colleague.

rationales.The colleague I sent the timetable to ha: The preposition moves to the end, and the object relative can be omitted: I sent the timetable to that colleague.
rationales.The colleague who sent me the timetable: This makes the colleague the sender of the timetable rather than its recipient.
rationales.The colleague whose timetable I replied: This changes a reply from the colleague into the speaker's response to a timetable.
rationales.The timetable that my colleague sent has: This shifts the described head to timetable and reverses who sent it.

sentence: The applicant who was interviewed first has accepted another job.
setupText: Choose what the relative clause tells us about the applicant.
taskText: The applicant who was interviewed first has accepted another job.
text: Choose what the relative clause tells us about the applicant. The applicant who was interviewed first has accepted another job.
options: The applicant received the first interview.
The applicant conducted the first interview.
The applicant accepted the first job offered.
The applicant interviewed someone in another job.
answer: The applicant received the first interview.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3178:Passive subject relative and modifier scope
explanation: Who was interviewed first identifies the applicant by being the first person interviewed.

rationales.The applicant conducted the first interv: Was interviewed is passive: the applicant received the interview rather than conducting it.
rationales.The applicant accepted the first job off: First belongs to the interview order, not to the order of job offers.
rationales.The applicant received the first intervi: Who was interviewed first identifies the applicant by being the first person interviewed.
rationales.The applicant interviewed someone in ano: The relative clause concerns the applicant's own interview; another job belongs to the main clause.

sentence: Describe the customer as the person I spoke to.

explanation: That can refer to a person in a defining relative; who I spoke to would also be valid.

rationales.The customer that I spoke to her has lef: That already represents the person after to; her repeats the object.
rationales.The customer whose I spoke to has left a: Whose needs a possessed noun and cannot introduce I spoke to alone.
rationales.The customer where I spoke to has left a: Where refers to a location, but the customer is the person addressed.
rationales.The customer that I spoke to has left an: That can refer to a person in a defining relative; who I spoke to would also be valid.

sentence: Some emails contain invoices. Print those emails, and leave the others unprinted.
setupText: Choose the sentence that identifies which emails to print.
taskText: Some emails contain invoices. Print those emails, and leave the others unprinted.
text: Choose the sentence that identifies which emails to print. Some emails contain invoices. Print those emails, and leave the others unprinted.
options: Print the invoices that contain emails.
Print the emails before they contain invoices.
Print the emails whose invoices have been removed.
Print the emails that contain invoices.
answer: Print the emails that contain invoices.
focusKey: coverage-relative-clauses-b1-3180:Defining relative in a selective instruction
explanation: That contain invoices restricts the command to the required emails.

This reverses the container relationship: invoices are inside the emails, not the other way round.
That contain invoices restricts the command to the required emails.
rationales.Print the emails before they contain inv: Before introduces a time relationship rather than identifying the emails by their current contents.
rationales.Print the emails whose invoices have bee: Removed invoices are no longer contained in those emails, so this selects a different group.
